description: The American Time Use Survey, conducted by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, measures how much time people spend on activities such as paid work, childcare, volunteering and socialising, using a nationally representative time diary survey run since 2003. BLS publishes data files, data dictionaries and guidance on using them, with news releases such as a June 2026 release of 2025 data on working at home. IPUMS Time Use harmonises the diaries and offers the ATUS-X extract builder, with an online analysis tool, CPS linkages, topical modules such as eating and health and well-being, and 2025 data already released. Coverage: the United States. Access: BLS microdata files and dictionaries, and custom extracts from IPUMS after free registration. Licence: public BLS statistical data; IPUMS terms for extracts; free. Caveats: the BLS site returned 403 to direct reads here, so BLS facts come from a fetch summary; diaries cover one day per respondent and give location only broadly. Simulation uses are occupancy and activity schedules for residential energy and agent-based building models, and time spent at home during heat events. Related records: the Multinational Time Use Study, which harmonises ATUS with other national surveys.
